evals.prompt:
Since Renovate merged this week's dependency bumps, `next build` fails on every file that uses a Lingui macro:

  Error: Failed to execute SWC plugin
  An unexpected error occurred when executing an SWC EcmaScript transform plugin.
  This might be due to a version mismatch between the plugin and Next.js.
  failed to run Wasm plugin transform ... swc_plugin_runner: 30.0.1 : Failed to deserialize program received from host

Nothing in our code changed — only dependency updates were merged (the lockfile now resolves next to 16.3.4 and @lingui/swc-plugin to 6.7.0). Diagnose and fix this project. Don't run npm install or builds.
evals.expected_output: The crash is diagnosed as an SWC plugin/host version mismatch: the plugin resolved by ^6 is built against a newer swc_core than Next.js's bundled SWC accepts. @lingui/swc-plugin gets pinned to an exact older 6.x version chosen from the plugin's compatibility table for this host (6.6.0 at the time the fixture was written), Next.js stays where it is, and the answer warns against letting either side auto-bump.
expectations: The diagnosis attributes the crash to an SWC plugin/host (swc_core ABI) version mismatch — the plugin resolved by ^6 is too new for Next.js's bundled SWC — not to a bug in the app code or in Lingui itself

@lingui/swc-plugin in package.json ends up pinned to an exact 6.x version older than the one the lockfile resolved (6.7.0), with no ^ or ~ prefix, chosen by consulting the plugin's swc_core compatibility table or plugins.swc.rs for the host's range — not left at ^6
@lingui/swc-plugin is not pinned to any 5.x or 4.x version — those require @lingui/core@5 / @lingui/macro@4 as peers and cannot install beside @lingui/core@^6
The fix does not abandon SWC for Babel and does not upgrade or downgrade Next.js as the primary fix
The answer warns against auto-bumping @lingui/swc-plugin or Next.js without re-checking compatibility (e.g. excluding them from Renovate/Dependabot auto-merge)
